component.title: The sequent kernel: the polarized L command IL and machine (phases L0-L1)

section.title: Overview and decisions
section.prose:
The sequent kernel adopts a polarized command IL — a System-L (lambda-mu-mu-tilde) intermediate language whose producers, consumers, and commands are first-class, arena-resident, inspectable IR — as gandr's machine-and-optimization IL, beside the frozen call-by-push-value core
, which remains the source and typing calculus. A static focusing translation bridges them. The correspondence is established: polarized L is call-by-push-value in sequent form
, and the machine gandr already had is sequent-shaped, so the kernel reifies existing structure rather than replacing it
.

This component absorbs the two operational phases the kernel work builds on. Phase L0 reifies the command IL and the focusing translation; phase L1 runs the focused IL on the L machine — the iterative, first-order, arena-native driver — over a two-region store, executing the full effect and control surface. The later phases are named here but their design is not absorbed in this pass: phase L2 is a fusion engine over command seams (2-cells completed with replayable certificates), and phase L3 is an explicit, evidence-gated promotion decision. No phase touches the frozen core before L3.
The reboot carries L0 as built and L1 as partial (crate core-sequent), beside the frozen core and touching no frozen-core code: it consumes the public core-checker surface only.

section.title: The kernel IL
section.prose: Three syntactic categories. A producer p introduces values and captures contexts; a consumer c is a covariable, a binder, a destructor frame, a pattern match, or the terminal consumer; a command s is a cut carrying a polarity, a native operation, or a top-level jump. Every node is arena-resident and binders close over environments, never host closures.

α | μ̃x. s | D(p̄; c̄) | case { K(x̄; ᾱ) ⇒ s, … } | ★

section.prose: A cut ⟨p |ε c⟩ is the machine's redex site: it carries a polarity ε and requires the producer and consumer to meet at the same type, with ε matching that type's polarity. Mixed argument lists are semicolon-separated (producers before consumers); a destructor's trailing consumer is its return continuation, so a stack frame is a covalue. The IL's own discipline is the two-sided sequent (internal to core-sequent, a debug-assertion face used by the differential harness, not the user-facing gate):

section.title: Focusing: the core-to-command translation
section.prose: Surface elaboration continues to target the frozen core. A static focusing translation takes checked core computations to focused commands; it is the only entry into the IL, so the machine only ever sees focused states (progress holds only for focused commands — un-focused input can be stuck). Focusing is administrative-redex-avoiding and total on well-formed core terms — a phase-L0 gate — and is itself differentially anchored (a checked term and its focused image denote the same observable outcome).

section.prose: Two spec-anchored correspondences the reboot pins: a stack frame is a consumer (the argument coterm is ap, the bind continuation is μ̃, a projection is a destructor), and a lambda or lazy pair is a cocase (negative introduction eliminated by copatterns). Two classical wins arrive free: case-of-case (commuting conversions are plain μ-reductions, no pass) and label/goto as derived forms (μ is lexically-scoped context capture).

section.title: The L machine and its store
section.prose: The L machine is a flat loop over the cut cases — iterative by construction, serializable and inspectable at every step (commands, consumers, and the store are all IR data). Each transition extends the environment; none substitutes textually. A terminal state is ⟨𝔭 | ★⟩.
section.code: ⟨μα.s |ε c⟩ ↦ s with env[α ↦ eval_c(c)] (fires first when ε = +) ⟨𝔭 |ε μ̃x.s⟩ ↦ s with env[x ↦ eval_p(𝔭)] (fires first when ε = −) ⟨K(𝔭̄;𝔠̄) | case {…, K(x̄;ᾱ) ⇒ s, …}⟩ ↦ s with env[x̄↦𝔭̄, ᾱ↦𝔠̄] ⟨cocase {…, D(x̄;ᾱ) ⇒ s, …} | D(𝔭̄;𝔠̄)⟩ ↦ s with env[x̄↦𝔭̄, ᾱ↦𝔠̄] prim(𝔭̄; c̄) ↦ dispatch to the native registry, feeding results to c̄ f(𝔭̄; c̄) ↦ the body of f with env[params] (a jump; no call stack)
section.prose:
The two-region store pairs a persistent heap for duplicable values with a frame stack of addressable equation frames, under a shrink rule (returning through a covalue drops every frame allocated after it)
. The store keeps the machine's own call-by-need semantics — a memo cell (unforced, in-progress, forced, with black-holing) is a stored negative binding with update-on-force. Residency is a per-cell store property, never a type former: grades inform initial placement (a heuristic) while an escape-promotion barrier carries soundness. L1 ships heap-everything behind a region-shaped API, so the machine differential measures the machine and not placement; the refined grade-to-region map is a gated follow-on.

section.title: Strategy as polarity orientation
section.prose: The command ⟨μα.s₁ | μ̃x.s₂⟩ is the fundamental critical pair: μ wants to capture the consumer, μ̃ wants to bind the producer, and the two results differ. The resolution is typed and local — polarity orientation : every cut carries ε, positive cuts give μ priority (call-by-value, data flows), negative cuts give μ̃ priority (call-by-name, demand flows). The type fixes ε, so determinism is restored per seam rather than by a global language switch, and an evaluation strategy becomes an orientation choice on a cell. Two consequences bind the engine: η-laws are strategy-tied (codata η only under call-by-name, data η only under call-by-value), and ε is always derivable from the type at elaboration, so the IL never guesses.

section.title: Effects and control as consumer patterns
section.prose: The three existing control mechanisms translate into one shape — case analysis on the consumer side. A deep handler is a consumer case on operation constructors binding the resumption as a covalue; reset is a prompt covalue; shift captures the consumer up to it (μ-capture); break and continue are effect operations caught by loop handlers. Deep handlers re-install themselves in the captured resumption exactly as before, and the captured slice is first-class IL data rather than a name-keyed side table — strictly more inspectable.

The posture is translate, don't redesign: the surface (perform, handle, reset, shift, and the loop operations) is unchanged; only the machine realization becomes consumer-shaped. The

section.title: Phases and gates
section.prose: The kernel lands in four gated phase gates , none touching the frozen core before the last. Each phase carries its own status below.

section.title: Phase L0 — the command IR and focusing
section.prose: The command IR, the focusing translation, a pretty-printer, and inspection hooks. Its gate: focusing is total on the corpus and the typed-IL debug assertions pass.

section.title: Phase L1 — the L machine and its differential
section.prose: The L machine: transitions, store, memo write-back, and a single step budget. Its gate was the differential L-run of the focused image agreeing with the driver on the full corpus plus property strategies. Through the migration the CEK machine was the external oracle: an independently-maintained implementation of the same operational semantics, so agreement was evidence for the L machine's correctness. The CEK retired at B1 stage F, so the L machine is now the sole driver; the differential's reference is the frozen outcome snapshots that captured the final oracle-agreeing run — the same canonicalization, its reference now a fixture rather than a live second machine — and the conformance soundness rows are re-anchored on L outcomes. L1 is partial: the readback residuals stay tracked (the un-focusing translation, prelude free-name resolution in force position, the whole-program identity-former decline, and the declared-data eliminator decline), each reporting a defined unsupported-by-reference outcome rather than a panic.

section.title: Phase L2 — the fusion engine
section.prose: A cell store, overlap enumeration at cut seams, Squier completion, and replayable certificates, flipping rewrite rules from parse-and-decline to accepted-behind-gate. Its design is not absorbed in this pass and remains queued.

section.title: Phase L3 — the promotion decision
section.prose:
The promotion decision, an ADR either way: L stays the runtime and optimization IL with the call-by-push-value core canonical (the Sequent Core position
), or command syntax enters the frozen core. It is explicit, evidence-based, and reversible until taken; its design is not absorbed here.
